name: Home Assistant Connect ZBT-2

radios.note: Silicon Labs MG24 at 2.4 GHz with an ESP32-S3 as USB bridge. Runs Zigbee 3.0 or Thread firmware, not both; no Bluetooth or Z-Wave. No model number is stated. Sold in North America, Europe (incl. UK retailers), Australia and Asia.

apple_home.note: Reachable only through Home Assistant software, which is not a hub; not confirmed.

google_home.note: Reachable only through Home Assistant software; not confirmed.

alexa.note: Reachable only through Home Assistant software; not confirmed.

home_assistant.note: Official Home Assistant hardware and its recommended Zigbee adapter: Zigbee through ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT, Thread through the OpenThread Border Router.

hubRequired.note: Not confirmed by an official source.

localControl.note: Home Assistant says Zigbee and Thread give devices a local connection, but no official page states local control for the adapter in so many words.

hubType.note: Successor to the ZBT-1; it replaced that model, which is discontinued.

deviceProtocols.note: One at a time: you pick Zigbee or Thread during setup and can switch later.

matterBridge.note: Not a bridge; Matter devices on Thread are reached through Home Assistant's Matter integration.

threadBorderRouter.note: With Thread firmware and the OpenThread Border Router in Home Assistant; the maker says it cannot be a standalone border router on its own.

summary: Replacing the discontinued ZBT-1, the ZBT-2 is a USB radio with a Silicon Labs MG24 chip. You pick Zigbee 3.0 (ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT) or Thread (OpenThread Border Router) during setup, one at a time per adapter. It is official Home Assistant hardware, and Home Assistant is the only ecosystem confirmed.

sources.title: The best gets better - Home Assistant Connect ZBT-2

caveats: It runs Zigbee or Thread, never both on one adapter.
Alone it cannot act as a Thread border router; that needs the OpenThread Border Router in Home Assistant.
ZHA allows one instance, so two ZBT-2 adapters cannot both run under ZHA.
